mmCompileSection.recompile_the_selected_: Recompile the selected flavor (this Image Size and Detection Batch) even if that engine already exists. Other flavors of the model are never touched.
mmCompileSection.select_model_rows_above: Select model rows above, set the sliders, then Compile. Builds on THIS machine's GPU (minutes each). Native TensorRT builders shipped for sm_120 / sm_89 / sm_86; other GPUs fall back to PTX (slower first compile).
manageModelsModal.which_server_the_model: Which server the model list and downloads come from. huggingface.co is the original; hf-mirror.com is a free mirror with the same files, reachable from mainland China without a VPN. When huggingface.co cannot be reached at all, ChitraMaya retries on hf-mirror.com by itself.
mmAddSource.title: Add a Hugging Face repo URL
mmImgszRow.detection_resolution_the_engi: Detection resolution the engine is built for - a multiple of 32 (YOLO stride). Higher (e.g. 960) downscales the frame less, so small or faint mosaics detect better, at the cost of slower compile and detection and more VRAM. 640 is the tested default; 960 suits dense VR content. Each Image Size / Detection Batch pair is compiled as its own engine flavor and kept beside the others; a run picks the flavor matching the panel's Image Size, so you can keep a 640 and an 800 engine of the same model.
mmLogCopy.title: Copy the whole compile log to the clipboard (CM-109)
mmDetBatchRow.detection_engines_are_buil: Detection engines are built for batch 1 up to this value and accept that batch or lower. A run picks the compiled flavor whose batch covers the panel's Detection Batch; if none does, the largest one runs and the run clamps to it and says so in the console. Each Image Size / Detection Batch pair is its own engine flavor, kept beside the others. 8 matches the panel's default.
mmMaxClipRow.as_of_v1_60.title: As of v1.60 restoration engines are clip-size independent: one compile serves every Max Clip Length setting (the dial in the Restoration panel now only costs memory at runtime). There is nothing to choose here any more.
mmNoCompileNote.tensorrt_engines_are_nvi: TensorRT engines are NVIDIA-only, so the compile section above is greyed on this edition: the models run in PyTorch as they are. An Intel compile path (OpenVINO) is under study; AMD has no Windows equivalent yet.
mmStdRun.title: Downloads the four models every install needs (lada detection v2 and v4 fast, zelefans VR detection v2 accurate, lada restoration generic v1.2) - skipping any already in models/ - and, on the NVIDIA edition, compiles their engines for the panel's Image Size and Detection Batch. Uses the Download via endpoint below. Shows Done when everything is present and compiled; press again after changing Image Size or Detection Batch to add that engine flavor.
mmUpAdd.title: Pick a .pth / .safetensors super-resolution model; it is copied into models/upscalers and identified. Usable models (RGB in and out, 2x to 4x) appear in the Secondary and Upscale Scaler dropdowns; anything else is listed with the reason it was skipped.
mmUpOpen.title: Open models/upscalers in the file manager.
mmUpRemove.title: Take the selected model out of the dropdowns. The file is moved to models/upscalers/_removed, never deleted - you fetched it once, you should not have to fetch it again.
mmUpRescan.title: Re-identify every file in the folder (the index is cached per file).
mmUpSection.weights_travel_content_never: Weights travel; content never does. Models are your own files (OpenModelDB lists hundreds, each with its own licence). Attention-based models (ATD, DAT, HAT, SwinIR...) are marked slow: seconds per region on a 3060.

presetHint.text: A saved configuration is the complete settings file — every control plus the output and temp folders. To load one, pick its name from the ⚙️ menu: one click applies it and makes it the active configuration. Files live in the presets folder next to the app and can be copied between machines.

cdToggle.title: Show/hide the console log — everything ChitraMaya prints (batch plans, skip reasons, recovery banners, watchdog alarms)
ctrlCodec.title: Output codec. AV1 needs an RTX 40-series (Ada) or newer to ENCODE (30-series can only decode it); ~30% smaller files than HEVC at the same quality, and previews play in the app without any HEVC extensions.
sectEncoder.constant_quantization_parame: Constant quantization parameter. Lower = higher quality, larger file (0-51)
sectEncoder.encode_on_a_background.title: Encode on a background thread so NVENC overlaps detection and restoration. Measured: no gain with NVENC -- 4-5 % SLOWER at both 1080p and 4K (the encode is ~15 % of the run and the thread competes with the restorer), identical output. Worth trying only when the encoder is the bottleneck (a software encoder or a CPU-bound machine). Adds a ~500-600 MB frame queue at 4K, which an 8 GB card cannot spare. Leave OFF.
sectEncoder.nvenc_speed_quality_preset.t: NVENC speed/quality preset. P1 fastest … P7 best quality
sectEncoder.where_the_per_run.title: Where the per-run files go: the run report (.run.json), its console log (.log) and the timecodes file (.timecodes.txt). Beside the video = next to the output (default); Temp folder = in the Temp folder; Off = not written at all. The app's own console log in the program folder is not affected.
sectMaskPreview.add_mosaic_sfw_censor.ti: Add Mosaic (SFW censor): instead of restoring, PIXELATE each detected region. Uses the selected Detection model (e.g. the NSFW model); no restoration model needed. Test Frame, Restore and Restore & Save all run in this mode — output is saved as -censored.mp4. Mutually exclusive with Preview Detection.
sectMaskPreview.fast_coverage_check_inst: Fast coverage check: instead of restoring, fills each detected region with a flat colour (set below) so you can see exactly what the detector found - without waiting for restoration. Any mosaic still visible is a detection miss; adjust Score or Image Size. Mutually exclusive with Add Mosaic.
sectMaskPreview.flat_fill_colour_for.tit: Flat fill colour for detected regions
sectMaskPreview.mosaic_cell_size_in.titl: Mosaic cell size in pixels for Add Mosaic mode (bigger = coarser blocks).
sectMaskPreview.upscale_no_restoration_d: Upscale (no restoration): decode, scale, encode - nothing else. No detector, no restorer, no tracker; the Detection and Restoration sections grey out except Output Upscale, Upscale Scaler, Scaler Quality and Scaler Denoise, which drive the scaler. For content that has nothing to restore and that you want at a higher resolution (a 720p or 1080p file for the headset). Set Output Upscale to a target or factor; with it Off this is a plain re-encode with the Encoder settings. Restore becomes Upscale (the marked segment, then Preview shows it), Restore & Save becomes Upscale & Save (the whole video), output -upscaled. Test Frame does not apply. Mutually exclusive with Add Mosaic and Preview Detection.
sectMosaicDetection.detector_input_resol: Detector input resolution (multiple of 32). Higher (e.g. 960) downscales the frame less, so small or faint mosaics detect better, at the cost of slower detection and more VRAM. 640 is the tested default; 960 suits dense VR content. With Use Tensor on, the compiled engine must match this size - if it doesn't, the run falls back to PyTorch at this size and the log tells you to recompile at the new size in Manage Models.
For VR studios that apply the mosaic in VIEWING space: blocks look square in the headset but arrive warped in the raw frame, which detection and restoration handle poorly. Fisheye warps each eye so those blocks become square again, analyzes there, and warps only the restored regions back - background pixels are never resampled. Leave Off for content whose mosaic already looks square in the flat player (most studios). Requires Split SBS.
sectMosaicDetection.how_confident_the_de: How confident the detector must be to accept a mosaic (0.05-1.00). Lower catches more, including faint or partial mosaics, but risks false positives on mosaic-like texture; higher is stricter. 0.20 is the default; lower it if mosaics are being missed, raise it if clean skin gets boxed.
How many frames the detector processes per GPU call (1-16). Higher is faster but uses more VRAM - lower it if detection runs out of memory. Affects only speed and memory, not quality. 8 is the default and what Manage Models compiles engines for; a run clamps to the engine's batch and says so.
Side-by-side stereo (VR): split each eye, detect separately, merge, and keep restorations from crossing the seam.
sectMosaicDetection.after_the_run_the.ti: After the run, the detector looks at the finished video (one key frame every couple of seconds) and reports the frames where mosaic is still visible, in the console and in the run report. This is how you learn about a region the detector missed during the run or a rim the restorer did not clear; open a listed frame with Test Frame. Costs well under 1% of the run time. Off = skip the scan.
sectMosaicDetection.use_fp16_precision_f: Use FP16 precision for detection (selects the fp16 detection engine)
sectMosaicDetection.use_the_compiled_ten: Use the compiled TensorRT engine for detection if available (faster). Unchecked = PyTorch .pt.
sectMosaicDetection.when_two_detections_: When two detections overlap, how much overlap is allowed before they are merged into one (NMS). Lower merges more aggressively into fewer, larger boxes; higher keeps more separate boxes. Rarely needs changing from ~0.70.
sectMosaicRestoration.blend_the_restored: Blend the restored patch using the detector exact pixel outline of the mosaic (segmentation mask) instead of its rectangular box. On = cleaner edges that follow the mosaic real shape; off = the whole box is blended. Leave on unless the mask looks wrong.
sectMosaicRestoration.extra_cleanup_pass: Extra cleanup pass on upscaled regions (RTX Super-Res modes only; Real-ESRGAN is unaffected). Chains a second Maxine pass in DENOISE mode after the upscale, so pasted regions come back cleaner - most visible on large regions and in VR viewing. Loads a second Maxine effect (extra VRAM) - on 6 GB cards weigh it against the run's headroom. Approach ported from jasna (AGPL), with credit.
sectMosaicDetection.widen_every_detected: Widen every detected region by N pixels on each side (0-64) before tracking and restoration. The detector often stops one row of mosaic blocks short of the true edge, especially where a hand or another body part cuts across the mosaic; the margin covers that row. It adds no detections and cannot fix a mosaic the detector missed entirely. One block row is about 15 px at 1080p and 30 px at 4K. 0 = off.
sectMosaicRestoration.how_many_consecuti: How many consecutive frames the restorer processes together as one clip - this IS the model's temporal window, so longer clips give smoother, more stable motion but use more VRAM. As of v1.60 engines are clip-size independent: with Use Tensor on the dial is free up to 720 on one compiled set (past ~180, wall time stops improving and only memory grows). With Use Tensor off (PyTorch) the dial is free up to 600. On both paths the only ceiling is memory - a too-long clip stops with a clean out-of-memory error; dial down and retry (the restoreChunkFrames config entry can also cap the PyTorch window without shortening clips). Independent of detection.
sectMosaicRestoration.how_the_restored_p: How the restored patch is blended back into the frame. Face Swap (default since 1.80) = the blend follows the mosaic actual shape: every mosaic pixel is fully replaced and a soft edge runs OUTWARD into the surrounding skin (width set by Feather), so there is no rectangle and no rim - usually cleaner, especially on SBS/VR content. None = a rectangular blended region (can leave a hard ice-block edge around the mosaic); kept for A/B. (Blending scheme adapted from Rope's face-swap compositor.)
sectMosaicRestoration.limits_the_size_at: Limits the size at which each region's crop is kept in VRAM while its scene is open. Off (recommended): crops are kept at native size, which gives the restorer everything the frame has - on 4K close-ups that can be 3,500-px crops and several GB per open scene, more than an 8 GB card holds. A cap downscales crops larger than N px at capture, so a scene costs at most Max Clip x N x N. It costs some fine skin texture on the regions it touches (the restorer works from a 256-px view of the crop either way, but a downscaled crop reaches it smoother). Leave Off unless the VRAM preflight in the console advises a value or a 4K run stops out of memory; 1024 is the gentlest, 512 the smallest. Applies only to crops above N px; smaller regions are untouched. The run report lists the frames affected (frames.capped).
sectMosaicRestoration.sharpens_large_res: Sharpens large restored regions. Restoration works on a 256-px crop; regions bigger than that get stretched at paste-back and look soft - worst on VR close-ups. A secondary scaler upscales the restored crop 2x or 4x with real super-resolution first, so paste-back shrinks instead of stretching. Regions smaller than 256 px are untouched. RTX Super-Res (NVIDIA Maxine) needs an RTX GPU and a recent driver and uses about 1.5 GB extra VRAM. Real-ESRGAN (bundled model, no downloads) works on every GPU - NVIDIA, Intel Arc, and AMD. Applies only to real restoration (not Preview/Add Mosaic). If unavailable the run continues without it and says so in the log. Your own models: a .pth or .safetensors super-resolution model in the models\upscalers folder (RealPLKSR, SPAN, ATD, ESRGAN and more; 2x to 4x) appears here by name and upscales the restored crop by its own factor; the same list serves the Upscale Scaler below.
sectMosaicRestoration.smooths_per_frame_: Smooths per-frame restoration/upscale shimmer (fizzle, wiggly fine detail) by averaging each restored frame with its 6 temporal neighbors where the content agrees - real motion and lighting changes pass through untouched. Runs on restored regions only; the rest of the frame is never modified. Uses the vs_temporalfix model (tiny, ~2 MB); needs its .pth weights next to the restoration model or in models/. Strength 1 is the default; 3 may give better results and takes more time (2 costs the most for the least). Too high may soften very small movements. Real restoration only.
sectMosaicRestoration.soften_the_edge_wh: Soften the edge where the restored patch meets the original frame by N pixels (0-64). The feather runs outward from the mosaic outline into clean skin (the mosaic itself is always fully replaced), fading over about 2xN pixels (half strength at N). Higher hides the seam for a smoother blend. 0 = auto: 2.8% of the frame height (60 px at 4K, 30 px at 1080p), so the blend band is the same width on screen for a small region and a large one - on a small region the fade is capped by what its crop can hold. Applies when Blend Mask = Face Swap. With Blend Mask = None it has no effect. Frame-proportional width from jasna (AGPL), with credit.
sectMosaicRestoration.upscale_every_fini: Upscale every finished frame before encoding, to a factor (2x, 4x) or a target height (1080p, 1440p, 2160p; the aspect ratio is kept, a source already at or above the target runs without the upscale). Scaler models are fixed 2x/4x, so a target like 720p to 2160p runs the scaler and resamples the result to the exact size. This is a whole-frame stage, separate from the Secondary scaler that only touches restored regions. Cost depends on the Upscale Scaler below: Real-ESRGAN runs its network on every output pixel of every frame (about 0.5 s per 1080p frame on a 3060 - clips, not titles); RTX Super-Res is built for video and far faster. Limits: H.264 stops at 4096 on a side (2x of 1080p is fine; 4x needs HEVC or AV1), HEVC/AV1 at 8192 - a request past the limit runs without the upscale and says so in the console. Applies to real restoration and to the Upscale mode (not Preview Detection / Add Mosaic); Test Frame stays at the source size. With Async Encode on, the queued frames are larger.
sectMosaicRestoration.use_fp16_precision: Use FP16 precision for restoration (selects the fp16 engine set)
sectMosaicRestoration.use_tensorrt_engin: Use TensorRT engines for restoration (much faster). Unchecked = PyTorch. Needs compiled sub-engines for this model + precision + clip size.
sectMosaicRestoration.where_decoded_fram: Where decoded frames wait for paste-back. Auto (recommended): on NVIDIA, Re-decode -- no frame store at all; a second decoder produces each frame again when it is due, so Max Clip Length costs no RAM or VRAM and no full frame crosses the PCIe bus. On AMD/Intel, Auto keeps the frame store: GPU VRAM when it fits, system RAM when it would not. Device forces VRAM (the classic behavior); Host forces system RAM; Re-decode forces the second decoder (NVIDIA; Split SBS yes, VR Projection and Test Frame keep the store).
sectMosaicRestoration.who_decodes_the_so: Who decodes the source on the AMD and Intel editions (NVIDIA uses NVDEC and ignores this unless NVDEC declines a stream). Auto (recommended): the GPU's video decoder through ffmpeg (Intel QSV, else D3D11VA), frames handed to system memory; the CPU stays free for the rest of the run. Off: ffmpeg decodes on the CPU - slower on 4K and on weak CPUs, but the decode path that never produced a bad frame. Why the choice exists: on AMD the D3D11VA hand-over can occasionally deliver a frame that was not finished (black from a row down, or green when only the colour was missing). The decode guard catches those frames, completes them from the previous frame and lists them in the run report (frames.frame_repair); Off avoids them outright. CM_HW_DECODE in the environment overrides this setting.
sectMosaicRestoration.which_model_scales: Which model scales the whole frame when Output Upscale is on. Real-ESRGAN: the bundled realesr-general-x4v3 compact model, every GPU vendor, slow (a fixed 4x network on every output pixel). RTX Super-Res: NVIDIA Maxine VideoSuperRes on the full frame - native 4/3, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4x, built for video streams, fast enough for whole titles; Scaler Quality and Scaler Denoise above apply to it. Needs an RTX GPU and the nvidia-vfx package; when Maxine cannot take the size, the run falls back to Real-ESRGAN and says so in the console. Your own models: drop a .pth or .safetensors super-resolution model (RealPLKSR, SPAN, ATD, HAT, DRCT, SwinIR, ESRGAN, Compact and more; 2x to 4x) into the models\upscalers folder and it appears here by name - OpenModelDB lists hundreds, each with its own licence. A 2x model reaches 2160p from 1080p in one pass and from 720p in two; the run report carries the ms/frame of whichever model ran. A file that is missing or fails to load falls back to Real-ESRGAN with a console note.
sectMosaicRestoration.when_a_region_stay: When a region stays on screen longer than Max Clip, its clip is cut and the next one starts cold - the restorer has no run-up on the first frames after a cut, which shows as a pulse or seam every Max Clip frames. Overlap N re-restores the last 2xN frames of the cut clip as the lead-in of the next one, so both clips have context at the seam; the first N frames of the lead-in are discarded (the earlier clip's result stands there). Costs 2xN extra restorer frames per cut - about +22% restorer time on long scenes at Max Clip 90 / Overlap 8, less at longer Max Clip. Short scenes cost nothing. 0 = off (hard cuts). Design from jasna (AGPL), with credit.
sectMosaicRestoration.with_overlap_on_fa: With Overlap on, fade from the earlier clip's result to the next one's over a few frames at the seam (Overlap / 3 frames each side) instead of switching in one frame. Uses frames that are restored anyway, so it is free. Off = a hard hand-off at the seam. Needs Overlap > 0.
sectMosaicRestoration.quality_level_of_t: Quality level of the RTX Super-Res upscale itself (NVIDIA Maxine's Low / Medium / High / Ultra). High was the fixed setting before 1.80. Higher levels reconstruct more detail and cost more time and VRAM per upscaled region; the effect is only visible on regions larger than 256 px (the ones the scaler touches). RTX Super-Res modes only; Real-ESRGAN has no quality level and ignores this.
